title: WHY CANADA GOOSE CHICKS FOLLOW SO CLOSE

narration_timeline.text: Why do these tiny Canada goose goslings stay so close to the adults?
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic Canada goose family with visible goslings.

narration_timeline.text: A young goose cannot fly yet, so its family travels together on land and water.
narration_timeline.scene: Downy Canada goose family moving together.

narration_timeline.text: The chicks peck for food on grassy banks while other geese move beside them across the lake.
narration_timeline.scene: A gosling foraging on grass followed by separately filmed Canada geese at a shoreline.

narration_timeline.text: In a different scene, more goslings explore their surroundings while they are still learning to move around.
narration_timeline.scene: Separate 2015 USFWS footage showing goslings; do not claim a continuous family or adult protective action. Actual motion/framing must be confirmed in rendered video before release.

narration_timeline.text: Adult geese can glide across open water, while their young still need to stay nearby.
narration_timeline.scene: Real adult Canada goose swimming on Golden Gate Park lake; not presented as the same family.

narration_timeline.text: For now, the safest path for a little gosling is right beside its watchful family.
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic Canada goose family and gosling footage from separate originals, without pretending a continuous event.
